scope: Independent design/plan source review only; no implementation or Julia admission

findings.title: Make the failed-row norm guard explicit before fallback readiness
findings.evidence: Current src/simplex_recovery.jl:145 rejects unreliable refinement before dot(direction,direction) at146 and its finite/positive check at147. A zero direction with a zero correction can produce finite-unreliable unchanged quality; a finite huge direction can produce a nonfinite squared norm. The Task2 bullet61 classifier permits both unless it adds a norm gate; bullet60 and spec15 require rejection. The fallback work ledger currently names only a finite-direction scan.
findings.requested_change: Require exactly one existing-order dot(direction,direction) plus finite/positive check on an otherwise eligible unreliable row before returning fallback_ready=true; preserve reliable-row arithmetic/check order, avoid duplicate norm work, and add this O(m) reduction to spec/plan ledgers. Pin zero and overflow finite-unreliable controls in later tests. An alternate consistent design must explicitly resolve the invalid-norm exclusion instead.

unnecessary_work_memory_assessment: No unnecessary normal-path scans/solves/retained arrays are proposed. One necessary failed-row norm reduction is missing from the explicit eligibility and cost ledger. Default-mode scalar/boxing and allocations require the later planned measurements; no performance claim is accepted now.
